title: Why Speaking Softly Is An Effective Classroom Management Strategy anagement-strategy/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin makes the case that lowering one's voice, rather than raising it, is a more effective way to command student attention and cooperation. He explains that a loud, commanding tone reads to students as nagging or as a sign the teacher doubts their intelligence, which encourages them to tune out, while a soft, deliberate voice draws students in both physically and mentally. He details several effects of speaking quietly: students become still, lean in and watch the teacher, feel respected and therefore want to listen, become calmer, and begin to mirror the teacher's tone in their own interactions. He allows that passion and volume have their place during lessons and games, but recommends a quiet, controlled voice specifically for giving directions and handling behavior.
points: Lower your voice for directions and behavior correction rather than raising it.
Speak just quietly enough that students in the back must lean in to hear.
Recognize that a calm voice signals control and reduces classroom tension.
Expect students to mirror your tone - a loud teacher tends to produce a loud, chaotic class.
Save volume and intensity for lessons, motivation, and games, not routine directions.
quotes: Most teachers talk too loud. They turn up the volume because they believe that the louder they are the better their students will listen.
Students tune out teachers who bark commands and instructions. To them it sounds like nagging or threatening or that their teacher doesn’t think they’re bright enough to follow along otherwise.
It’s best to speak just soft enough that the students in the back of the room have to strain ever so slightly to hear you.
A calm, polite voice sends the message that you’re in control of the class and that you know exactly what you’re doing. This is a comforting, even soothing, notion to students.
What you do is more influential than what you say. So when you quiet your voice and speak politely to your students, they’ll do the same.
Stand in one place, look your students in the eye, and speak to them in a soft voice. Tell them exactly what you want.
